name: Limits

subjectOf.text: The availability of information generated through the dynamic feedback process cannot be optimized at any given point in time, because the feedback effect is intended to perpetually reinforce itself.
subjectOf.abstract: the availability of information generated through this process cannot be optimized at any given point in time.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560

subjectOf.text: The authors qualify their own case: stable cryptocurrencies can experiment with monetary policy on an unprecedented scale only because they are insulated from real world complexities and political positioning, and that advantage shrinks once real world market factors actually apply to them.
subjectOf.abstract: This allows them to experiment with monetary policy tools on an unprecedented scale. Such experimentation is limited if and when real-world market factors pertain to such stable cryptocurrencies.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396522
scope_conditions: applies as stable cryptocurrencies scale into real world use

subjectOf.text: Equal opportunity access points for public marketing incentives cannot be guaranteed and require constant reevaluation, so the public marketing permission for any fair token launch should be restricted to a limited percentage of total token supply.
subjectOf.abstract: These equal opportunity access points cannot be guaranteed and the process is subject to constant reevaluation. The public marketing permission for any fair token launch should be restricted to a limited percentage of total token supply.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: fair launch project grants public marketing incentives
